title: Buyer dislikes project density
buyer_primary_need: Avoid a crowded, privacy-poor feel, especially people passing the unit in shared lift lobbies and corridors.
key_information_learned: The buyer's main concern is lifts and corridors, not high-rise living categorically.
Block-specific lift banks help somewhat, but 15–18 units per typical floor remain a concern.
The buyer wants to inspect a typical floor plan and representative corridor before deciding whether the shared areas feel too busy.
The buyer is interested in viewing and asks about weekday or weekend slots, but has not committed to an appointment.

transcript.speaker: customer
transcript.message: 1846 units sounds too dense. I don’t like crowded condos.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.message: I understand — 1,846 units is a substantial total, so I wouldn’t describe Pearlmont as low-density. They’re across three towers; a typical floor has 15 units in Blocks 1B and 1C, and 18 in Block 1D, with four passenger lifts per block. That gives a clearer picture than the total alone, though it may still feel busy depending on what matters most to you. Is your main concern the lifts, shared facilities, or privacy?

transcript.speaker: customer
transcript.message: Mostly the lifts and corridors — don’t want it feeling like there’s a constant stream of people outside my unit. How are the access and lifts separated between the blocks?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.message: Each block has its own lift bank: 4 passenger lifts plus 1 Bomba lift per block, rather than one shared lift bank for all three. Residential parking and drop-off are also separated from the commercial access; residential drop-off is at Level 4, with link bridges to the towers. There are some connecting bridges between blocks too, so they’re not completely isolated. The lift setup is block-specific, but it can’t guarantee a quiet corridor on every floor.

transcript.speaker: customer
transcript.message: Block-specific lift banks help a bit, but 15–18 units on a floor still sounds like quite a lot. Do you have a typical floor plan showing how the units are arranged around the lifts?

transcript.request: Please verify whether a customer-shareable typical floor plan is available for the residential blocks, showing how units are arranged around the lift lobby and corridors. Include any verified block-specific differences.

judge.strongest_ai_move: The Agent acknowledged the density concern without trying to dismiss it, asked one focused question that revealed the buyer's specific concern, and later used support to offer a relevant way to inspect the layout while clearly stating that it could not predict crowding or noise.
judge.weakest_ai_move: The turn 2 response gives several access and lift details at once. They are relevant and supported, but could have been slightly more concise before checking whether the information addressed the buyer's concern.

The floor-plan/corridor viewing information came from a SIMULATOR_SYNTHETIC_VERIFIED_FIXTURE, not Pearlmont factual Knowledge or evidence of a real live operational connection.
judge.improvement_recommendation: No material correction is indicated. Keep the turn 2 factual response focused, and continue distinguishing a buyer's interest in checking options from acceptance of a specific appointment time.
